$comment: Publisher plugins installed directly because they carry more than skills (hooks, a language server, sub-agents, commands). Their pure skills are vendored under skills/ instead. catalog.py renders this list on the README and the catalog site.

plugins.name: superpowers
plugins.why: Planning, TDD, debugging and subagent-driven development methodology.
plugins.why_plugin: A SessionStart hook bootstraps the skills; copying the skills alone drops it.

plugins.name: dotnet
plugins.why: C# refactoring and local SDK setup, plus C# language-server integration.
plugins.install: claude plugin marketplace add dotnet/skills && claude plugin install dotnet@dotnet-agent-skills

plugins.name: differential-review
plugins.why: Security-focused review of a diff with git-history context.
plugins.install: claude plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills && claude plugin install differential-review@trailofbits

plugins.name: sharp-edges
plugins.why: Finds error-prone APIs and dangerous configuration defaults.
plugins.why_plugin: Its skill delegates to the sharp-edges-analyzer sub-agent.
plugins.install: claude plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills && claude plugin install sharp-edges@trailofbits

plugins.name: insecure-defaults
plugins.why: Audits a codebase for hardcoded credentials, fallback secrets and fail-open settings.
plugins.why_plugin: It is a /insecure-defaults:audit command with a JS workflow, not a skill.
plugins.install: claude plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills && claude plugin install insecure-defaults@trailofbits
